text: For oplog-dependent initial sync and CDC workflows, size source retention to preserve the history each workflow still needs: MongoDB says a logical initial sync restarts if it finds an oplog gap during oplog application and requires a window covering those apply phases; Percona ClusterSync, which uses change streams, says sync fails when needed source oplog operations expire before processing; AWS DMS says its task fails if oplog records expire before DMS reads them. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md ; https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/oplog-sizing.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MongoDB.html

AWS DMS documents MongoDB data-shape constraints that can block or narrow a migration: table mode requires consistent types for each field and does not replicate fields absent from target columns; its homogeneous MongoDB-compatible flow does not support inconsistent _id types or time-series collection migration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.MongoDB.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/dm-data-providers-source-mongodb.html

A MongoDB logical initial sync used to seed a destination can restart from the beginning if a gap is found in oplog continuity because the source oplog window is too short to cover the apply stage; the target also needs disk space in the local database to buffer oplog records during the data copy. MongoDB documents these conditions. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync/

Relational-to-MongoDB document construction can fail when legacy records contain null or missing values, failed numeric conversions, or incomplete relationships; a value with the expected shape can still be factually wrong. MongoDB schema validation enforces configured field types and ranges, but shape validation alone cannot establish historical truth. (medium confidence) Sources: https://gonzalosimon.hashnode.dev/migrating-data-without-trusting-the-data ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/schema-validation.md

A MongoDB change-stream consumer used for migration CDC cannot resume from a token whose event has fallen out of the participating oplog; MongoDB reports ChangeStreamHistoryLost for that condition. A cross-cloud migration case report describes monitoring resume-token health and lag, disk use, and source-to-delta document counts while bulk copy and change capture ran together. (medium confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/docs/change_streams.md ; https://www.haptik.ai/tech/migrating-terabytes-of-mongodb-across-clouds-with-minimal-disruption

Network interruption handling differs by tool: MongoDB native initial sync may resume after temporary network errors, but persistent errors restart it from the beginning; Percona ClusterSync documents that its initial sync is non-resumable and restarts from scratch after failure. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync/ ; https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/limitations.html

MongoDB documents a rare mongosync embedded-verifier false positive: differing document field order across source nodes can make verification fail even when mongosync copied the documents correctly. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Verification needs to match the workload and collection features: MongoDB says document-count comparison only verifies successful sync for insert-only workloads, while the embedded verifier skips capped, TTL-indexed, and non-default-collation collections; MongoDB also describes checks across documents, views, and indexes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/verification.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/verification/embedded.md

Percona ClusterSync requires the same major MongoDB version on source and target and does not synchronize users, roles, or system.* collections; a migration that assumes full-cluster copying must provision this state separately. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-08)
